branch_provenance.syndrome: Chronic Progressive Multifocal Hypopigmented Macular Lesions with Absence of Hair Growth

state.case_summary:
A man in his 40s presented with a 2-year history of multiple asymptomatic lesions on the face and neck. The lesions were round, hypopigmented macules and were symmetrically distributed in the affected area. The macules had appeared on his cheeks 2 years earlier and had gradually coalesced. The size of the lesions ranged from approximately 2 to 3 mm to 25 mm in diameter. There was no hair growth at the site of the lesions, and the patient reported no symptoms. He was previously treated for tinea versicolor, without success.

Multiple round, hypopigmented macules symmetrically distributed on face and neck. Lesions ranged from 2-3 mm to 25 mm in diameter. Absence of hair growth in affected areas.

- Skin Biopsy Results:    - Histopathologic findings showed plate-like subepidermal tumor extending horizontally under epidermis with multiple cord-like connections to overlying epidermis    - Neoplastic cords consisted of clear/pale epithelial cells with cytoplasm showing strong periodic acid-Schiff staining due to glycogen accumulation    - Stroma formed by fibrous connective tissue    - Marked elastosis observed in dermis surrounding tumor  Images:    Image A Title: Hypopigmented macules on the face and neck    Image B Title: Absence of hair growth in the affected area    Image C Title: Hematoxylin-eosin staining (original magnification ×10)    Image D Title: Hematoxylin-eosin staining (original magnification ×20)
